newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Siemens seen blazing Eurobond trail.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Siemens seen blazing Eurobond trail.

text.p: German industrial giant Siemens AG , by launching Eurobonds that will later convert to euros, may have blazed a trail for other companies planning financing under a single European currency.

Siemens on Tuesday launched Eurobonds in marks, guilders and French francs that will be redenominated in euros after the third stage of European economic and monetary union, scheduled for January 1, 1999.
"For large benchmark issuers, this may well become some form of norm," said Paul Hearn of Siemens syndicate mangaer J.P. Morgan in London. "There are a lot of people looking at these ideas."
Bonds like this "give investors a way to take different views on EMU across different markets, depending how positive they are on EMU," Hearn told Reuters Financial Television.
Siemens treasury chief Christian Weller von Alefeld told RFTV the company expected EMU to begin on time, but was not concerned about a delay.

"We feel, as the market is expecting, that the euro will go ahead," he said. "We will then be able to redenominate our franc, guilder and mark bonds, reconsolidate them, and have a rather liquid Eurobond, maybe even as a benchmark out there."
If EMU is delayed, "we keep the bonds as they are," Weller said. "We are not involving ourselves in the EMU discussions publicly."

Hearn agreed EMU is not crucial for the success of the issues. "The critical thing in the first place is the deals have to work on a stand-alone basis in the market," he said. "Provided they are well priced, EMU is not an imperitive."

J.P. Morgan and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell were joint arrangers on all three deals. Dutch bank ABN AMRO Hoare Govett was the joint lead manager on the guilder bond. French bank Paribas was involved on the franc deal.
Bankers said the offering was one of the strongest selling they had ever seen.

The bonds were a 750 million mark offering to be priced at a yield spread of 17 basis points over German government bonds, with a 2.5 billion franc deal to be priced 14 basis points over French OATs. A 500 million guilder deal was to be priced 20 basis points over Dutch DSLs.
